title: Meet the CPU
about: What cores really do, and why the CPU needs to stay cool.

cards.prompt: Saving a video takes 12 seconds. Add cores to reach 3.
cards.explanation: A video is lots of separate frames, so the cores share them. One core takes 12 seconds; four take 3.
cards.hint: This job splits into frames, so each extra core takes a share. Watch the timer.
cards.nudge: Keep adding cores and watch the timer drop. It has to reach 3 seconds or less.

cards.title: More cooks in the kitchen
cards.body:
A **core** is one worker in the CPU. Four cooks chop vegetables four times as fast, but four cooks can't bake a cake any sooner.

Cores only help a job that **splits into pieces** that don't wait for each other.

cards.explanation: Photos and frames are separate pieces, so cores share them. A clue hunt or knitting needs the step before, so extra cores wait.
cards.hint: For each job, ask: does every piece need the piece before it to be finished?
cards.nudge: Separate pieces can be shared out. If each step needs the step before, extra cores just wait.

cards.prompt: A job can't be split. Both laptops same speed. Which wins?

options.nudge: A job that can't split runs on one core. Extra cores don't make that core quicker.
Extra cores only help a job that splits into pieces. This one can't.

cards.explanation: A job that can't split runs on one core, whichever laptop. Same speed, one core each, so they finish together.
cards.hint: Think of the cooks: can extra cooks help a job that can't be split?

cards.prompt: Hard work heats the CPU. Tap each part.

parts.job: The CPU does all the work. Hard work makes it hot.
This copper heat pipe carries the CPU's heat away to the metal fins.
The fan blows air through the fins and out the vents, cooling the CPU.

cards.explanation: The CPU gets hot. The heat pipe carries its heat to the fins, and the fan blows it out the vents.

cards.title: A real heat pipe

photo.alt: Inside a laptop: copper heat pipes curve from the processor area to a round fan.

cards.caption: Real **copper heat pipes** run from the processor (hidden under the plate) to the **fan**.

cards.sentence: **Throttling** is when a CPU gets too hot and slows itself down to stay safe.

cards.prompt: Tap the **CPU** and the two parts that cool it.
cards.explanation: The heat pipe carries heat from the CPU, and the fan blows it out the vents. Block the vents and the CPU throttles.
cards.hint: Three parts: the small shiny chip, the copper pipe, and the part that moves the air.
cards.nudge: Tap all three: the CPU, the copper pipe carrying its heat, and the fan.

cards.prompt: This laptop is throttling. Stop it slowing down.
cards.explanation: Off the blanket, the vents breathe and the CPU stops throttling. Cleaning a dusty fan means opening the laptop: ask an adult or repair shop.
cards.hint: What traps the heat, and what stops the fan cooling? Fix both.
cards.nudge: A hot CPU slows itself down. Clear the blanket and clean the fan so the heat escapes.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **Cores** only help jobs that split into pieces.
- A hot CPU **throttles**: it slows down to stay safe.
- The **heat pipe** and **fan** keep it cool.

**Try this:** use a laptop on a hard surface, not a bed, so its vents stay clear.

**Next:** put it all to the test in the module quiz.
